title: Zscaler's ARM template for an NSS VM in Azure

prose.text: For VM-based NSS on Azure ([[shared.nss.servers]]), Zscaler publishes an Azure Resource Manager template. It builds the NSS VM and its networking, and leaves the NSS server record, certificate and feeds to the Admin Console ([[shared.nss.feeds]]).

prose.label: Before deploying.
prose.text: {{sas-token}} {{vhd-regions}} {{mgmt-ip-no-sku}} Whether it can be deployed where Basic SKU addresses are unavailable is open {{gap:mgmt-ip-basic-sku}}.

checks.do: Whether the deployed NSS VM's inbound access has been restricted from the template's open default.
Which VHD region and SAS token a deployment needs, especially for Azure Government.
Whether the target subscription and region allow Basic SKU public IP addresses, because the template's management IP is created without a SKU.

creates.statement: The NSS ARM template creates two network interfaces (management and service), a NAT gateway, two public IP addresses and a public IP prefix, a virtual network with two subnets, a network security group, a storage account, an automation account and one virtual machine.

interfaces.statement: The NSS VM's primary interface is the management interface and carries a public IP address; the second interface is the service interface, on a private subnet behind a NAT Gateway.

quotes: The primary interface is used for management and carries a public IP address.
The second interface is used for service purposes, and is placed on a private subnet behind a NAT Gateway.

nsg-open.statement: The template launches NSS but the operator must modify the network security group to secure inbound connections; the sshSourceAddressPrefix parameter defaults to '*', which allows SSH from any IP and is not recommended for production.

quotes: launch NSS, but at this time, you are required to modify the Network Service Groups (NSGs) to properly secure inbound connections based on your environment
Default '*' allows access from any IP (not recommended for production).
Source IP address or CIDR range allowed for SSH access.

sas-token.statement: Deployment needs an NSS VHD SAS token for the chosen region, obtained from Zscaler Support, and each VHD region requires its own dedicated SAS token.

quotes: Contact [Zscaler Support](https://help.zscaler.com/login-tickets) to obtain the NSS VHD SAS Token for your selected region
Each region requires authentication via a dedicated SAS Token.
providing the name of the region where you want to download the VHD image from

vhd-regions.statement: The VHD source region is selectable: znssprod (US Commercial), znssprodeu (Europe) and znssprodau (Australia) for commercial Azure, and zsgovnsstexas, zsgovnssarizona, zsgovnssiowa and zsgovnssvirginia for Azure Government; a government region in a commercial account is not supported and fails the deployment.

quotes: Choosing a government region for deployment in a commercial Azure account is not supported and will cause the template deployment to fail.

vm-sizes.statement: The template's allowed VM sizes are Standard_D2_v4 (default, 2 vCPUs and 8 GB), Standard_D4_v4 (4 vCPUs, 16 GB), Standard_D8_v4 (8 vCPUs, 32 GB) and Standard_D16_v4 (16 vCPUs, 64 GB).

disk-copy.statement: The template uses an Azure automation account runbook to copy the new NSS OS disk into the new or existing storage account, which takes about 20 to 30 minutes because the VHD is about 500 GB or more; the deployment must not be cancelled once started.

quotes: The template uses an Azure automation account runbook to make a copy of the new NSS OS Disk, and stores it in the newly created or existing storage account.
The template takes about 20-30 minutes to deploy due to the VHD image size (~500GB+). Do not cancel the deployment once started.

image-version.statement: Release 1.0.5 of the template (December 3, 2025) was updated to support NSS VHD image 5.2.0, and the template's source VHD file name is znss_5_2_osdisk.vhd.

quotes: Updated template to support latest NSS VHD image 5.2.0

support.statement: Support for the ARM template is exclusively through GitHub issue tracking on its repository.

quotes: Support for this ARM template is made available exclusively through Github repo issue tracking.

mgmt-ip-no-sku.statement: In the template the management public IP (`<vmName>-MGMT-IP`) is declared with `publicIPAllocationMethod` `Dynamic` and no `sku`, while the service public IP (`<vmName>-SRVC-IP`) takes its `sku` from the `publicIpSku` parameter, whose default is `Standard`, and is `Static`. Issue #12 reports that selecting a Standard SKU still fails at the management IP with the Azure error that no more than 0 IPv4 Basic SKU public IP addresses can be created for the subscription in that region; it was open when captured.

quotes: "Cannot create more than 0 IPv4 Basic SKU public IP addresses for this subscription in this region."
as much as we select a standard sku for public addressing we get the following error when trying to deploy the MGMT-IP

mgmt-ip-basic-sku.title: Whether the management public IP can be deployed in a subscription without Basic SKU quota
mgmt-ip-basic-sku.detail: Issue #12 was open with no reply when captured. The template gives the management IP no SKU, so Azure creates a Basic SKU address, and a subscription and region with a zero Basic quota fails the deployment. The reporter's belief that Basic SKU public IPs are deprecated is theirs and no captured source states it. A workaround such as adding a Standard SKU and Static allocation to that resource is untested here.
mgmt-ip-basic-sku.blocks: deploying the NSS template into a subscription and region with no Basic SKU public IP quota

quotes: As far as I know the Basic SKU has now been deprecated.
